title: The 15-minute routine for new words (no app) | Words That Stick #5
description:
15 minutes a day. No app. Three new words is plenty.

• Minutes 0–5, anchor: write one sentence about your own life with each new word.
• Minutes 5–10, recall: cover the stronger word, read the everyday phrase ("very angry") and say the stronger word ("livid") before you look.
• Minutes 10–15, speak: say two new sentences with each word, out loud, as if you were telling a friend or a colleague.

Your turn: say one sentence about your week with "swamped", out loud. For example: "I was swamped at work this week."

No streaks to protect, no decks to manage. Just keep going.

5 ways to say "never give up", one picture each:
• keep going: a runner in the rain, still running
• determined: a girl who falls off her bike and gets straight back on
• tenacious: a little dog that won't let go of its rope toy
• relentless: waves hitting the rocks, again and again
• obstinate: a donkey that won't move, whatever you do (the bad kind: just stubborn)

Try it tomorrow: pick three new words and set a timer for 15 minutes.

More ways to say "never give up": https://anotherwordfor.net/never-give-up-synonym/

Next episode: why your mind goes blank.
